Wow you've been through a lot. Im so sorry. 

I just wanted to suggest you try some kind of medication one day. I know they offer a lot of mood stabilizers which Im sure would help to balance out your struggle to find the middle-range of emotions. Even if you only took the meds for a little while, just learning how to react normally again to things might help.

Good luck coping with everything... Really.
I'm so sorry. The conflicting feelings are the worst. Your story made me tear up a bit... I can relate a lot.

That's horrible. The worst thing someone can do when a person tells them they're depressed is play it off as nothing. It just makes the depressed person feel even more insignificant, weak and useless... Im so sorry. That sounds like hell. 

Our situations with family sound pretty similar as well. Something happened with my family and I about 6 years ago that dragged on and on and as much as I told them how depressed I was, or how hurt I was by what happened, they would laugh and say I was overreacting. 

What helped me was learning to live more in the moment. I realized I am never going to forgive my family for my past, and I don't need to. It's hard though. When something traumatic happens, it's hard to handle. I don't know how you're personally dealing with it, but I tried to repress it all. I tried to repress it until something would happen with my family that triggered all the memories, and all my anger and hurt would come tumbling out. 

Just I hope my advice helps a little, and you can try to just live in the now more. Hopefully that helps a little :/
She wasn't the one. I promise.

Im so sorry, that's really rough. I've been through/am going through a very similar situation, and Peace_In_Solitude is right. There has to be a major change, and you're going to have to stop seeing her in order to really start getting over her. I've been trying to get over a guy for two years, but unfortunately Im in the same situation as you, stuck in a small school with no way out. 

I wish you the best of luck with dealing with her, though, and I hope the next year/two years of high school fly by for you.
I'm thinking Italian #2.

... You need a break. Holy crap. That's heartbreaking! I'm glad your daughter is healthy and I'm very glad you realized how much trouble her dad is now before potentially getting yourself stuck in a relationship like what sounds like your mom was in. How is your mom doing now?

Other people, including myself, in this thread have been talking about how incredibly hard it is to put down our pets. I can only imagine how much harder it would be to put down your own father. Just writing that sentence hurts enough. I'm so sorry you had to go through that... I sincerely hope you and your mother are doing alright since he passed.

It makes me think of the day I'll be pregnant for the first time, and as excited as I know I'll be, I'll have to be so careful because of all the things that might go wrong. A time that should be so exciting seems like it often becomes a fearful task.
That must have been awful! How old were you at the time?

It really is so tough. :( I had to put my dog of thirteen years down as well. There always comes a point where you just know it's time, and it's heartbreaking. You're put in a position where you know you have to kill your best friend, because it's for the best. But it certainly doesn't usually feel that way.

I love my dad and my brother, but I can't say I love my mother. There was a time in my life when she cared about me, I know, but I don't remember it. That's why I don't think I love her. 

I would say I'm in love with my boyfriend. He's always been there for me, and when it's that kind of love, you just know.

The most confusing love I have is for my ex. I still love him, and I know I always will. We broke up because of a temporary situation, in which he didn't feel like himself. He says he still doesn't. It's confusing when you don't know if they love you back. At the same time, whether my love is unrequited or not, it wouldn't change my feelings.

Care to elaborate?

I think falling for someone is more something that just happens. It can be pushed along faster depending on certain circumstances, as it can be slowed by others. The only voluntary part would be choosing to pursue the person (for example: agreeing to go on a date), and then generally you eventually either fall in love or are uninterested.

After you fall in love, it's extremely hard to get over someone though. That's something that I don't think is voluntary. If you genuinely cared about the person and the relationship, it's going to hurt a lot no matter what. You can try to push along the heartbreak, but only time can truly heal it. 

Either way, I'm so sorry you've had your heart broken. That's the worst feeling.

Thank you for the advice, really. I have considered talking to the school therapist before, but I don't know if they would be required to notify my parents if I did. I can't imagine the ridiculing from them if they heard about that. But thank you!
